subject: RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing — CloudNova SKU mapping & burst plan
messages:
From: Aisha Pate <procurement@cloudnova.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <eng@cloudnova.com>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@cloudnova.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP details: dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of CloudNova's RFP we need a detailed breakdown of how Redwood recommends sizing a dedicated pool for our main ML workloads. High level: a mixed workload of 1) real-time chat completions (mostly 8k tokens, p99 latency target ~200ms), 2) batch rerank/embedding jobs (large batches overnight), and 3) occasional fine-tuning/parameter-efficient updates.

Can you provide: 1) recommended GPU SKUs and counts for reserved capacity, 2) expected throughput (tokens/sec and concurrent sessions) per SKU, 3) suggested burst lanes/overage strategy, and 4) any assumptions on quantization/mixed precision that materially change sizing?

We attached our current traffic shape (see CloudNova_Traffic.csv) to the RFP packet; happy to walk through. Timeline: we'd like Redwood's sizing workbook and written assumptions by next Thursday to feed procurement.

Best,
Aisha
Procurement Lead, CloudNova

--
Attachment: CloudNova_Traffic.csv (CSV, 98KB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Pate <procurement@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP details: dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire

Hi Aisha,

Thanks — we can do that. I've attached our Dedicated Sizing Workbook (single-sheet summary + detailed tabs) and a GPU-fitment heatmap image that maps model families and token-length profiles to SKU recommendations. Key assumptions in the workbook:
- Workload split: 62% chat (p95 gen length 2.4k tokens, p99 ~8k), 30% embeddings/rerank (batch windows), 8% fine-tune jobs.
- Latency target for chat: p99 <= 220ms (we recommend designing at 200ms for headroom).
- Models: primary serving on an L2-optimized variant (H100/80GB quantized for throughput; fallbacks to A100/40GB for cost tiers).
- Quantization: 8-bit (NF4) paths supported for non-finetune inference — reduces per-token GPU memory & increases packing efficiency; fine-tune paths use fp16.

Preliminary SKU mix (reserved pool recommendation):
- 8 x H100-80GB equivalent (reserved) — handles sustained high-concurrency and largest chat spikes
- 12 x A100-40GB equivalent (reserved) — cost-efficient baseline for steady traffic and embeddings
- 6 x L4 (or equivalent) for lightweight embedding replicas and dev/test burst lanes

Burst strategy: reserve a tiered burst lane (on-demand capacity with guaranteed cold-start <60s) and an overage automatic fallback to a slightly smaller quantized model to preserve latency SLOs. Workbook includes throughput per-SKU for common model types (tokens/sec at 2k and 8k seq lengths) and concurrency maps.

We have a few clarifying questions inline in the workbook, but below are the main areas we'd like you to confirm to finalize numbers:
1) Do you have hard p99 latency objectives for the embeddings jobs (or is throughput more important)?
2) Overnight batch windows: are you open to elastic transient capacity (spot/rental) for cost savings?
3) Any corporate constraints on specific GPU vendors or region-only preferences?

If the timeline works we'll target a refined workbook by 2027-09-16. Ben will run the throughput validation and Marissa will draft the procurement-ready summary.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Solutions — Dedicated, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_v1.xlsx; gpu-fitment-heatmap.png
From: Michael Chen <eng@cloudnova.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Pate <procurement@cloudnova.com>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@cloudnova.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP details: dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire

Naomi — thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications after a quick pass through the workbook: 
1) For chat we care about end-to-end p99 under typical user prompt lengths (2k) and heavy long-form sessions (8k). We are ok with a model fallback if it stays within 15% quality delta.
2) Embeddings batch: target is to finish nightly rerank within a 4-hour window; throughput matters more than p99 latency there.
3) Fine-tune jobs: we do periodic LoRA-style updates that require checkpointing and the ability to run longer-lived jobs (several hours).
4) Vendor constraints: procurement prefers vendor-agnostic SKU language but our security team flagged that some customers require avoidance of select regions with older NVLink topologies — can Redwood map recommended SKUs to both H100-family and an A-architecture fallback?

Also: what does Redwood recommend for a 12-month commit vs 36-month commit in terms of pool sizing elasticity? We want to understand safe commit % to avoid overpaying.

Will you and Ben be able to include a simple cost delta table (reserved vs on-demand burst) and an ops playbook for failover?

Thanks,
Michael
Senior ML Platform Engineer, CloudNova
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <eng@cloudnova.com>, Aisha Pate <procurement@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP details: dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire — follow up & recommendations

Michael / Aisha —

Appreciate the clarifications. Summary of final recommendations and answers to your items below. Ben and I validated throughput numbers in a staging run against representative models; we've baked the results into the workbook (linked above) and attached a short procurement summary.

1) Latency and fallback: design for p99 <= 200ms at 2k and target p99 <= 320ms for 8k (measured at service edge). We recommend an automatic model-fallback policy (H100 -> A100-quantized -> smaller L2-quantized) that keeps quality within your 15% delta constraint while remaining within latency SLOs.

2) Embeddings batch window: to finish within 4 hours we recommend reserving enough A100-40GB baseline capacity to complete 1.2x your expected batch volume, and use transient burst (rental/on-demand) for the rest — this gives a good balance of commit cost vs peak speed. Workbook tab 'BatchSizing' shows specific GPU-hours per job.

3) Fine-tune jobs: reserve a small pool of H100s for checkpoint-heavy runs (we recommend 2 reserved H100s and a 4-node burst lane for peak days). Long-running fine-tune tasks should be scheduled into maintenance windows where possible.

4) Vendor/regional mapping: yes — the workbook includes two fitment mappings: H100-class (preferred) and A100-class fallback SKU descriptions. We avoid referencing cloud vendor SKUs directly in contract language; procurement summaries use 'H100-equivalent (80GB)' and 'A100-equivalent (40GB)'.

5) Commit guidance: for a 12-month commit we suggest reserving ~70% of steady-state baseline (the 'safe commit' number in the workbook). For 36-months, a 85% commit is defensible if you commit to an established, predictable growth runway. We included a sensitivity heatmap (attachment: gpu-fitment-heatmap.png) that shows risk vs savings across commit percentages.

6) Cost delta & ops playbook: included in the workbook and in the procurement summary doc. High-level: reserved capacity reduces per-token cost materially (~25–35% depending on SKU mix); burst/on-demand margins depend on region and spot availability — we provided conservative estimates. Ops playbook covers routing policies, automatic fallback rules, escalation contacts, and a runbook for late-night batch overruns.

Next steps: we can 1) lock in a joint review session (30–45m) to walk the workbook, or 2) provide a procurement-friendly one-pager for your legal/finance teams. Which do you prefer?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Solutions — Dedicated, Redwood Inference
